How to track car registration and insurance renewals
How to track car registration and insurance renewals
Note the kind of paper, the date and where it is kept, then look six weeks ahead so a renewal does not sneak up. Check your state for its rules.
5 min read
Updated 26 September 2026
In this guide
9
sections
For each car, write down four things on the day a new paper arrives: what it is, the date it runs out, where the paper is, and how it renews. Look at the list once a month and act on anything inside six weeks. That covers registration, insurance, inspection and a warranty.
This is for US drivers who want the dates in one place. It can't tell you what your state requires, how much a renewal costs, or when a lapse becomes a violation. Those live with your state motor vehicle agency and your insurer, and this isn't legal advice.
An example tracker with made-up dates.

How to set it up
Put the paper in front of you: registration card or renewal, insurance policy or card, any inspection report, the warranty booklet.
For each one, copy the end date printed on it. For insurance, that's the end of the policy term, not the date the bill is due.
Write where the paper lives, in words you'd understand in a hurry ('kitchen drawer, blue folder').
Write how it renews: mailed notice, online at your state's site, or automatic. Note the card on file if it's automatic.
Subtract six weeks from each date and put that in your calendar or on the list as the act-by date.
When a renewal comes through, write the next date that day, while the new paper is in your hand.
One renewal, week by week
Six weeks is our rule of thumb, not a legal one. Some renewals take a day and some take a month.
Six weeks out
Look for the notice. If none has come, find out why: an old address, a different insurer, an email in spam.
Four weeks out
Start the renewal. Book an inspection if your state needs one.
Two weeks out
Renewal should be paid or in the mail. If not, treat it as urgent.
The day it runs out
Check the new paper is in hand. Put the old one in the recycling.
The same day
Write the next date on the tracker.

Where this goes wrong
Most renewals slip for boring reasons. A move means the mailed notice goes to your old address, so update your address with your state's motor vehicle agency and your insurer at the same time. A switched insurer means a new term date, so change the tracker the day you switch. An automatic renewal fails when the card on file expires. Two cars with dates in the same month get treated as one job and one of them gets missed.
Insurance and registration are also linked in many places, and a lapse in one can cause trouble with the other. How that works differs from state to state, so look it up in yours instead of assuming. For the wider habit of catching yearly bills before they arrive, see

Questions people ask
How far ahead should I renew my car registration?
There's no single rule, and your state may have its own window. We'd start looking six weeks before the date, because a mailed notice, an inspection or a fee can each take time. Your state's motor vehicle site, found through USA.gov, says when renewal opens and what it needs.
Where do I find my car insurance renewal date?
On your policy declarations page or your insurer's app, as the end of the policy term. That can differ from your bill due date. Your insurer usually sends a renewal notice before the term ends, so if none arrives, call and ask.
Do I need to keep track of both registration and insurance?
Yes. They come round on different dates, are handled by different offices, and can affect each other. Put each on its own line with its own date, and write where each paper lives.
Can my state send me a renewal reminder?
Many states offer email or text reminders, and most mail a notice. Sign up on your state's motor vehicle site if it offers one. Don't rely on it alone, since notices go to old addresses and spam folders.
What if I just moved?
Update your address with your state's motor vehicle agency and your insurer, since a renewal notice goes to whatever address is on file. Rules on how soon you must change it differ by state, so check yours. Then update the tracker's 'where the paper is' line.
